import { Steps, Aside, CardGrid, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import SeqDiagram from '../../../components/SeqDiagram.astro';

When you ship a new version of your app whose **state shape changes**, the bytes
already stored in every app instance can no longer be read as the new layout. The
upgrade carries a **migration**: a transform that reshapes the app's existing
state into the new schema. The upgrade is an entry in the app's own log: the
leader runs the migration once, and the other replicas apply the state it wrote
([Upgrades & migrations](/protocol/upgrades/)).

This is the build-side how-to. For who may upgrade, how the migration is planned
from the two ABIs, and organization-wide upgrade runs, see
[Application upgrades &amp; migration](/protocol/upgrades/).

<Aside type="note" title="When you need a migration">
  Only when the **serialized shape** changes — adding/removing/renaming a field,
  changing a field's type, or struct↔enum reshapes. Adding a new method, a new event
  variant, or a pure bugfix that does not touch the layout needs only a version bump,
  not a migration body.
</Aside>

## Write the migration

<Steps>

1. **Bump the schema version.** Set the new version on your state struct:

   ```rust
   #[app::state(version = 2, emits = for<'a> Event<'a>)]
   pub struct AppStateV2 { /* ... */ }
   ```

2. **Author the transform.** Two ways — pick the derive for routine field changes,
   or hand-write for anything that needs logic.

   **Derive (`#[derive(app::Migrate)]`).** Declare the old type with `from =`, and
   annotate only the fields that change. Unannotated fields **carry** 1:1.

   ```rust
   #[app::state(version = 2, emits = for<'a> Event<'a>)]
   #[derive(app::Migrate)]
   #[migrate(
       from = AppStateV1,
       emit = Event::Migrated { from_version: SCHEMA_VERSION_V1, to_version: SCHEMA_VERSION_V2 }
   )]
   pub struct AppStateV2 {
       items: UnorderedMap<String, LwwRegister<String>>,   // carried (no attribute)
       #[migrate(new = LwwRegister::new("added in v2".to_owned()))]
       notes: LwwRegister<String>,                          // seed a new field
   }
   ```

   The field strategies:

   | Strategy | Field attribute | Result |
   |----------|-----------------|--------|
   | Carry (default) | *(none)* | `field: old.field` |
   | New field | `#[migrate(new = expr)]` | `field: expr` |
   | Rename | `#[migrate(from = old_name)]` | `field: old.old_name` |
   | Convert | `#[migrate(with = expr)]` | `field: (expr)(old.field)` |
   | Rename + convert | `#[migrate(from = old, with = expr)]` | `field: (expr)(old.old)` |

   A rename, from `apps/migrations/migration-suite-v4-rename-field`:

   ```rust
   #[migrate(from = description)]
   details: LwwRegister<String>,
   ```

   **Hand-written (`#[app::migrate]`).** For anything with logic — denormalizing,
   splitting a field, populating a new collection — read the old bytes with
   `read_raw()`, deserialize into a `...V1` struct, and build the new state.
   `read_raw()` returns the raw root-state bytes (`None` if no state exists) with the
   storage layer's 32-byte element-id suffix already stripped, so it deserializes
   straight into your old struct. From `apps/migrations/scenario-crdt-native-v2`:

   ```rust
   #[app::migrate]
   pub fn migrate_v1_to_v2() -> ScenarioCrdtNativeV2 {
       let old_bytes = read_raw().unwrap_or_else(|| {
           panic!("Migration failed: no existing state. Create a V1 context first.");
       });
       let old_state: ScenarioCrdtNativeV1 =
           BorshDeserialize::deserialize(&mut &old_bytes[..])
               .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("Migration failed: V1 deserialization error {e:?}"));

       app::emit!(Event::Migrated {
           from_version: SCHEMA_VERSION_V1,
           to_version: SCHEMA_VERSION_V2,
       });

       // Denormalize v1 keys into a new tags vector — sorted for cross-node determinism.
       let mut keys: Vec<String> =
           old_state.items.entries().unwrap().map(|(k, _v)| k).collect();
       keys.sort();
       let mut tags: Vector<LwwRegister<String>> = Vector::new();
       for k in keys {
           tags.push(k.into()).unwrap();
       }

       ScenarioCrdtNativeV2 { items: old_state.items, title: old_state.title, tags }
   }
   ```

3. **Guard it with a `#[app::migration_check]`.** This pre-commit predicate gets the
   deserialized `old` and `new` state and returns `bool`; `false` aborts the
   migration before it commits. Three built-in predicates cover the common
   invariants:

   | Predicate | Checks |
   |-----------|--------|
   | `entity_count_parity(old, new, delta)` | `\|old.count() - new.count()\| <= delta` — catches silent drops/dupes |
   | `no_orphaned_refs(refs, keys)` | every id in `refs` exists in `keys` — catches dangling references |
   | `conservation(old_total, new_total)` | `old_total == new_total` — catches off-by-one / drift |

   From `apps/migrations/scenario-migration-check-pass-v2`:

   ```rust
   #[app::migration_check]
   pub fn check(old: ScenarioMigrationCheckPassV1, new: ScenarioMigrationCheckPassV2) -> bool {
       let old_keys: Vec<String> = old.items.entries().unwrap().map(|(k, _v)| k).collect();
       let new_keys: Vec<String> = new.items.entries().unwrap().map(|(k, _v)| k).collect();
       entity_count_parity(&old_keys, &new_keys, 0)
   }
   ```

   A check can take an optional third `witness` parameter if your `#[app::migrate]`
   returns `(NewState, Witness)` and you want to assert against data the transform
   captured.

</Steps>

## The determinism rules

Write a migration as a **pure function of the old state**. It runs once, but
the SDK runs it in storage **merge mode** and refuses what would make its
result depend on the run rather than on the old state:

- **No clock, no randomness, no caller.** Derive every new value from the old
  state alone; `env::time_now()`, random sources and the executor's id have no
  place in a schema change.
- **Sort before you iterate into ordered structures.** Map iteration follows
  entity ids, not keys; if you fold map entries into a `Vector` or any
  positional structure, `sort()` the keys first (as the example above does) so
  the order follows the data.
- **Use the explicit mutators.** `Counter::increment` and `Rga::insert` read
  the executor id / HLC and **panic** inside a migration. Use their explicit
  siblings instead:

  ```rust
  counter.increment_for(&id)?;                      // not increment()
  rga.insert_str_at_timestamp(pos, ts, text)?;      // not insert(); ts non-zero
  ```

<Aside type="caution" title="Migrations run in merge mode">
  The runtime executes your migrate in merge mode and reassigns deterministic
  collection ids afterward, so newly created collections get ids derived from
  where they are stored. Treat a panic from a mutator as the SDK catching a
  migration that depends on who or when it ran.
</Aside>

## Authored / identity-gated data migrates per-owner

A whole-root `#[app::migrate]` reshapes the shared parts of your state, but it
**does not** convert `AuthoredMap` / `AuthoredVector` entries. Those are stamped
**per owner**, and only a call by the owner may rewrite them, so the root
migration — which runs as no owner — cannot touch them. They keep their old
schema until each owner upgrades their own entries.

To make that one tap, `#[app::state(version = N)]` auto-generates two extra exports
whenever your state declares at least one identity-gated collection:

| Export | Kind | What it does |
|--------|------|--------------|
| `migrate_my_entries` | call | Re-writes every entry the **caller owns** that is still below the target schema, routing through the owner-driven convert (re-stamps as the owner). Returns a `MigrateMyEntriesSummary { converted, remaining }`. |
| `count_my_pending` | read-only | Tallies the caller's still-stale owned entries without writing — drives the prompt below. |

`SharedStorage` is deliberately **excluded** from this sweep: it is an admin-rotated
writer-set with a different conversion model, not per-owner data.

<Aside type="caution" title="The root migrate does not finish the job">
  After deploying v2, do not assume every entry is on the new schema. Each owner's
  `AuthoredMap` / `AuthoredVector` entries stay at the old schema until **they**
  call `migrate_my_entries`. Surface `count_my_pending` in your app and prompt
  users with a non-zero count to run the one-tap migrate; re-offer "finish" until
  the summary's `remaining` reaches `0`.
</Aside>

<LinkCard title="Permissioned storage" href="/build/permissioned-storage/"
  description="AuthoredMap / AuthoredVector ownership, SharedStorage, and the identity-gated write model." />

## Roll it out

A migration ships inside a new release of your application. Moving an app to
that release (`meroctl context update`, or an organization-wide upgrade run) is
an entry in the app's own log, so every call before it ran on the old code and
every call after it runs on the new. The leader runs the migration and its
check; if either fails, the app stays on the old release and its state is
untouched.

- [Operate](/operate/) — publishing and installing a release.
- [Upgrades & migrations](/protocol/upgrades/) — who may upgrade, how the plan is
  chosen from the ABIs, and organization-wide runs.

    { from: 1, to: 1, label: 'migration_check passes' },
    { from: 1, to: 2, label: 'commit the upgrade entry: new bundle + new state' },
    { from: 1, to: 0, label: 'upgraded', dashed: true },
    { type: 'divider', label: 'every later call runs on v2' },
  ]} />

The scenarios under `apps/migrations/` are runnable end-to-end fixtures (add field,
remove field, rename, change type, struct→enum, CRDT-native, migration-check
pass/fail, and more) — the closest thing to a test suite for your own migration.
